title: Gogdara Rock Carvings
subtitle: Prehistoric petroglyphs and a Buddhist addition in Gogdara, a hamlet of Udegram, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Gogdara Rock Carvings
edits: The rock face is drawn (no source gives its size or shape): a cliff face about 11 m wide and 6 m high, bulged and roughened by hand, seated on the real DEM slope at the place point; the site is a rock face at the foot of the slope, not a levelled terrace (terrace 0).

The incised figures are drawn after photos Zainul Abideen and Yusra.Amin123 (Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0): a row of animal outlines with horns or necks, a few human-like figures, a spoked wheeled form, and dots and rings. Their number, size and places are estimated from the photos, not measured.
The sources give a chariot only in one line (Livius: 'the animals and chariots'); the drawn wheeled form is after that line and the photos, not measured.
The sources give 'more than 100 carvings' and 71 animals, 17 objects and 29 unidentified (Olivieri, via Dawn); the drawing shows a sample, not all of them.
The Buddhist relief (sixth century CE, Livius) is not visible in the photos used and is not drawn.
The face is turned to the end of the drive (no compass bearing is given in any source); the photos show the cliff, not its orientation.
The village lanes that bring the visitor here are OSM roads; the N-95 Mingora road is about 0.46 km off, so the drive takes the lanes from the junction and stops at the rock.
